summary: Market sentiment is cautiously bearish, rattled by a confluence of geotechnical tensions and corporate leadership uncertainty, with investors broadly de-risking amid elevated volatility signals. On the macro front, escalating Middle East conflict is dominating attention, as Houthi forces attacked a Saudi Aramco pipeline, four tankers were struck by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz, and an oil tanker was hit off the UAE coast, collectively threatening global energy supply chains and pushing crude prices higher. In equities, Nvidia shares are under pressure following Jensen Huang's departure, with succession concerns overshadowing the company's otherwise dominant AI positioning, while Cerebras surged 13% on strong earnings and a new Microsoft partnership, and Cisco rallied after reporting AI infrastructure revenue is set to double this fiscal year. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include Strait of Hormuz disruption and its potential to spike oil prices, the leadership vacuum at the world's most valuable semiconductor company, and widespread cloud infrastructure outages hitting Microsoft, AWS, and Google simultaneously, raising systemic reliability concerns. In the short term, markets face a difficult path given the layered risks of an energy supply shock, geopolitical instability across Iran, the Middle East, and ongoing US-Iran diplomatic breakdown, suggesting energy names may outperform while tech faces continued headwinds until Nvidia's succession and the cloud outages are resolved.
